prompt: A test calls $('id=example.tickets:id/refresh').click() against Tickets on the emulator. Which program performs the tap on the screen?
hint: Four pieces, and only one of them is on the device.

choices.text: The Appium server, on your computer
choices.why: The server receives the request and hands it to the driver; it never touches the screen.

choices.text: The driver's own app on the device
choices.why: Right. The UiAutomator2 driver installs a small server app there, and that app acts through Google's UiAutomator.

choices.text: WebdriverIO, which sends the tap through adb
choices.why: WebdriverIO speaks HTTP to the server and knows nothing of adb.

choices.text: Tickets, which reads the test's request
choices.why: Tickets has no idea it is being tested; nothing in its code listens for a test.

prompt: Match each piece of an Appium run to what it is.
hint: The table of section 02.

pairs.right: a client library, in the test's own process
a Node program listening on port 4723
the Android driver, a plug-in of the server
what the iOS driver puts on the device

right_distractors: the app under test, rebuilt for testing

prompt: A colleague says: Appium speaks one protocol for both platforms, so our Android suite will run against the iOS app once platformName says iOS. What is wrong with that?
hint: What does a locator name, on each platform?

choices.text: iOS does not use WebDriver, so the requests change
choices.why: The requests are the same; the XCUITest driver answers WebDriver like UiAutomator2 does.

choices.text: Nothing, apart from automationName
choices.why: The capabilities are the smaller half; the elements are named differently on each platform.

choices.text: The elements have different names on iOS unless both apps were built to agree
choices.why: Right. A resource id is Android's; iOS has accessibility identifiers, set separately by the developers.

choices.text: The suite needs Appium's iOS client library
choices.why: There is no separate iOS client; the same WebdriverIO drives both.

prompt: Why does the lesson start the server with npx appium --address 127.0.0.1?
hint: What did 0.0.0.0 mean in the first start?

choices.text: So that the emulator can reach the server
choices.why: The emulator never connects to Appium; the driver reaches the device through adb.

choices.text: Because Appium will not start without one
choices.why: It started without one in the same section, on every interface.

choices.text: To make each request reach the server faster
choices.why: Loopback is quick, but the reason in the section is who can reach the server at all.

choices.text: So nobody else on the network can open sessions
choices.why: Right. On 0.0.0.0 anybody who reaches port 4723 could install apps and read the screen.

prompt: On its first run, before JAVA_HOME was set, how many required fixes did the UiAutomator2 doctor report?
hint: The summary line that grep kept.

prompt: You install the fake driver while the server is running, and the first session for it answers: Could not find a driver for automationName 'Fake'. What fixes it?
hint: When does the server look at its drivers?

choices.text: Installing the driver again with npm install -g
choices.why: It is installed in the project already; a global copy is a second place for the version to live.

choices.text: Restarting the server
choices.why: Right. The server loads its drivers when it starts, so one installed later is not there yet.

choices.text: Writing appium:automationName with the prefix
choices.why: A missing prefix gives invalid argument, before any driver is looked for.

choices.text: Running npx appium driver doctor fake
choices.why: The doctor checks what a driver needs on the computer; it does not load the driver into a running server.

prompt: Put the requests of the session in section 04 in the order a test sends them.
hint: Nothing can be found before there is a session, and nothing clicked before it is found.
items: POST /session/{id}/element with a strategy and a value

prompt: The capabilities {"platformName":"Fake","automationName":"Fake"} were refused with invalid argument. Why?
hint: Which of the two names does the W3C define?

choices.text: automationName has no appium: prefix
choices.why: Right. platformName is standard; anything else needs a vendor's prefix, and Appium refuses it without.

choices.text: platformName needs the appium: prefix as well
choices.why: platformName is defined by the W3C, so it is written without a prefix.

choices.text: The fake driver had not been installed yet
choices.why: That gives a different error, about finding no driver; the names were refused before any driver was looked for.

choices.text: The body has to be sent as a form, not as JSON
choices.why: WebDriver bodies are JSON, and the request that worked sent JSON too.

prompt: A find answers no such element with the status 404. What, exactly, does that tell you?
hint: When did the server look?

choices.text: The app has no element with that id
choices.why: It may have one that was not drawn yet, or one on another screen, like remind.

choices.text: The session ended before the find arrived
choices.why: An ended session answers invalid session id, as section 04 showed after the DELETE.

choices.text: Nothing on the screen matched at that moment
choices.why: Right, and nothing more. Whether it would have appeared a second later is what a wait finds out.

choices.text: The driver does not know the id strategy
choices.why: An unknown strategy is a different error; id is the first one every driver answers.

prompt: A test crashed after creating its session and before sending DELETE. The next test, on the same real phone, waits and fails to start its session. What is the likeliest cause?
hint: What does the DELETE free?

choices.text: The crash uninstalled the app from the phone
choices.why: A crashed client cannot reach the phone at all; it only stopped talking to the server.

choices.text: adb forgets a device after a failed test
choices.why: adb knows nothing about tests; it keeps listing the device.

choices.text: The Appium server stops after any crashed client
choices.why: The server kept running; a client crashing is invisible to it until the session times out.

choices.text: The old session is still open and holds the phone
choices.why: Right. Until the idle timeout closes it, the device is busy with a session nobody is using.

prompt: Why does the test ask boxoffice for sh-103's seats instead of expecting the text 4 seats left?
hint: What happens to sh-103's seats when somebody places an order?

choices.text: The seats left depend on which tests ran before
choices.why: Right. Four is true after a restart and false after an order, while screen and API must agree either way.

choices.text: Appium cannot read a number from the screen
choices.why: getText reads any text, digits included.

choices.text: Tickets rounds the seats it shows
choices.why: Tickets prints seatsLeft as boxoffice sent it; Shows.kt does no arithmetic on it.

choices.text: To make the test finish sooner
choices.why: The extra request costs time; it is there for correctness.

prompt: In the recorded run with no device, how many seconds did the UiAutomator2 driver wait for a device on each attempt before giving up?
hint: The message gives it in milliseconds.

prompt: The driver gave up on finding a device after 20 seconds, yet the recorded run took 85 seconds to fail. Where did the rest go?
hint: Count the timestamped lines.

choices.text: node:test ran the failing test four times
choices.why: node:test ran the hook once; the report shows one test, failed in its hook.

choices.text: WebdriverIO asked for the session three more times
choices.why: Right. It retries a session that fails to start, about twenty seconds each; connectionRetryCount: 0 stops that.

choices.text: adb needed a minute to start its own server
choices.why: adb starts in a moment; the driver was asking it again and again for a device that was not there.

choices.text: The test waited for boxoffice, which was not running
choices.why: The fetch to boxoffice comes after the session, and the test never reached it.

prompt: On the model, $('~Refresh').isExisting() printed false, although the refresh button is there. Why?
hint: What does ~ ask for on Android?

choices.text: Accessibility id is a strategy for iOS apps and has no meaning on Android
choices.why: On Android it means the content description; it works on both platforms.

choices.text: Nothing in it has that description
choices.why: Right. ~ asks for an accessibility name, and the model, like Tickets, gives none.

choices.text: ~ needs the package name in front, like id=
choices.why: The package goes in front of a resource id, not of a description.

choices.text: The button is hidden in the model
choices.why: Only the banner and the error line are hidden; the button was found by id and clicked.

prompt: Which of these are reasons the lesson puts XPath last on Android?
hint: One reason is about change, one about cost.

choices.text: It describes positions, which move when the layout does
choices.why: Right. A designer who adds a row breaks every path that counted rows.

choices.text: The device has to write out the whole screen as XML to answer it
choices.why: Right. UiAutomator has no XPath of its own, so the whole tree is built and searched.

choices.text: UiAutomator2 does not accept XPath at all
choices.why: It accepts it; the XPath of section 06 found the third row on the model, and UiAutomator2 answers the same strategy.

choices.text: An XPath cannot name a resource id
choices.why: //*[@resource-id='…'] does; it is still slower than asking for the id directly.

prompt: A test does await driver.pause(5000) before tapping the third row. It passes on your emulator and fails on the slower CI device about one run in five. What is the fix?
hint: What is the test actually waiting for?

choices.text: Raise the pause to fifteen seconds
choices.why: It fails less and wastes fifteen seconds on every run, and a slower day breaks it again.

choices.text: Retry the whole test when it fails
choices.why: A retry hides the race instead of removing it, and doubles the time of a real failure.

choices.text: Wait for a row to be displayed, with a deadline
choices.why: Right. It returns the moment the list is drawn, on any device, and fails with a message when it is not.

choices.text: Add an implicit wait of thirty seconds as well as the pause
choices.why: Two layers of waiting multiply, and the pause still wastes five seconds every time.

prompt: To wait until a progress indicator has gone, WebdriverIO's waitForDisplayed takes the option { ___: true }.
hint: It turns the condition the other way round.

prompt: Where does the check that the seats equal what boxoffice reports belong?
hint: Who decides what the answer should be?

choices.text: Inside ShowScreen.seats(), so every test gets it
choices.why: Then every test that reads the seats carries one test's expectation, including tests that expect something else.

choices.text: In ListScreen.open(), right after the tap
choices.why: The list screen knows how to open a show, not what any test expects to find there.

choices.text: In the test itself, beside its other checks
choices.why: Right. The screen answers seats(); the test decides what the answer must be.

choices.text: In a helper that every screen object calls before it returns
choices.why: That is an assertion inside the screens again, one level further away.

prompt: A developer renames the resource id title to show_title. What do screen objects save you?
hint: How many times is the id written?

choices.text: The rename is found by WebdriverIO without any change
choices.why: Nothing finds a renamed id on its own; a changed id is a changed locator.

choices.text: Editing every test: only the screen classes change
choices.why: Right. The id is written once, in the screens, and the tests never mention it.

choices.text: Running the tests on the emulator at all
choices.why: Screen objects change how the code is arranged, not where it runs.

choices.text: The tests stop depending on Tickets's ids
choices.why: They still depend on them, through the screens; that is why the screens change.

prompt: A session request answers Could not find a connected Android device in 20000ms, and the emulator window is open in front of you. What do you check first?
hint: Who told the driver there was no device?

choices.text: curl localhost:4723/status
choices.why: It says the server is ready, which it was; it says nothing about devices.

choices.text: npx appium driver doctor uiautomator2
choices.why: The doctor checks the SDK and Java on the computer, which were fine; it never asks for a device.

choices.text: adb devices
choices.why: Right. The driver asks adb, so adb's answer is the one to see; an empty list means kill-server and look again.

choices.text: The capabilities, for a missing prefix
choices.why: A missing prefix is refused at once as invalid argument, before any device is looked for.

prompt: Match each error to the piece it points at.
hint: Section 02's four pieces, plus the locator.

pairs.left: All non-standard capabilities should have a vendor prefix
Could not find a driver for automationName
Could not find a connected Android device
pairs.right: the device, as adb sees it

prompt: The WebdriverIO script of section 06 ran cleanly against the fake driver and found every element it looked for by id. What has that proved about Tickets?
hint: Where did the elements come from?

choices.text: That Tickets has those resource ids
choices.why: The ids came from a model written by hand; Tickets could have been renamed since.

choices.text: Nothing about the app; only that client, server and protocol work together
choices.why: Right. The fake driver is a stand-in, and the model is only as true as whoever wrote it.

choices.text: That the list of Tickets loads within three seconds
choices.why: Nothing loaded; the model is an XML file read from disk.

choices.text: That the same script will pass on the emulator
choices.why: On the emulator it needs a built APK, a device and the real screen, none of which the fake had.

prompt: Put the setup of section 03 in the order that makes each step succeed.
hint: The doctor needs the driver, and the server loads drivers when it starts.
items: set JAVA_HOME, then npx appium driver doctor uiautomator2
